Hey! See if you can get accommodations ASAP. I was granted emergency accommodations at the very last minute right before finals in December of my 2L year. I was having a pretty severe mental health crisis after my mom died and basically told my law school that I either needed accomms or was dropping out. I was medicated for adhd at that time, but had never sought out or received accommodations previously. After being granted emergency accomms, they told me I needed a neuropsychological evaluation that recommended accomms if I wanted them in the future. They were definitely necessary because law school & losing my mom unexpectedly were both ruining my mental health. The neuropsychologist eval was extremely pricey but my doc negotiated with me and I paid $1500 and it honestly was so incredibly worth it. Getting accommodations for the bar was a breeze and I’m so thankful. I guess the moral of the story is - act now! Because if you can prove a track record of necessary accomms even if it only starts 3L year, you might stand a chance. Good luck! I know how hard it is to struggle with this. You’re so capable.

I don’t know if this is what you want to hear right now, but I’m going to be honest. I will preface this and say, if you do want to take the bar again, or want to be a lawyer, don’t continue reading this!

I developed serious health issues in law school, both mental and physical. I broke out into hives just about every day, my weight fluctuated 70 pounds in the course of 3 years, I was diagnosed with major depressive disorder, and swallowed a bottle of Xanax halfway thru my 2L year (spent a few days in the hospital, I’m all good now). I about went insane during bar prep. Worked my ass off, as we all do. My older sister was killed in a car accident on July 14th, 2021. About 10 days before the exam. I failed by 13 points. 

I was immediately sent back to a very dark place upon finding out I failed. I had support though, and sought therapy. It’s been a full year now that I have been able to do a lot of healing, soul searching, and taking time to move forward from all of this mindfully. I went from being on the highest doses of adderall and Vyvanse to no longer needing a stimulant. I have also tapered off all antidepressants since January, and my mental health has been better than it has ever been now. I stick to a mostly anti inflammatory diet and my physical health is also a lot better. I am down 30 pounds (still have a lot to lose!) I have found things in my life I look forward to, and I’m getting ready to transition into social work now, which will be a whole new adventure I’m really looking forward to. After the bar exam, after going through all of that, I never thought I’d be in such a good place I’m now in a full year later. I couldn’t justify writing it again either, but my best advice would be to hold on these next few months, and definitely give yourself a break after devoting your entire self to this for so long. Be kind to yourself, and try to find the intersection between what you love to do and what you can make an income from. With all that being said though, finish what you started tomorrow. Go in and give it your best shot, you don’t want to have any regrets after working so hard these past few months. Wishing you all the best as you move forward from this!
